date:healing-a-blind-man-at-bethsaida@2c.note: Mark 8:22 gives no date. The 29 AD year depends on dating outside Scripture.

date:the-demoniac@7a82e9.note: Mark 1:21 gives no date, only 'on the sabbath day'. The 27 AD year depends on dating outside Scripture.

near:golgotha_487>jerusalem_636@9931b8.note: 15:22 names Golgotha; 15:41 has the women coming up with him to Jerusalem. No distance is given, so 'near' is a reading.

occurred-at:3rd-tour-of-galilee>galilee_.note: 1:39 has him preaching throughout all Galilee. The text does not number a 'third tour', so linking the event to this passage is a reading.

occurred-at:fasting-question>capernaum_2.note: 2:1 places him in Capernaum and 2:15 has a meal 'in his house'. The fasting question names no place, so Capernaum is a reading.

occurred-at:healing-a-crowd-near-sea-of-.note: 7:31 says he passed through the coasts of Decapolis on his way to the sea of Galilee. The healing comes after, at the sea, not in Decapolis.

occurred-at:healing-multitudes>galilee_4.note: 3:7 has him withdraw 'to the sea' with crowds from many regions. Galilee is a reading; the verse does not name the place of healing.

occurred-at:healing-the-leper>galilee_43.note: 1:39 has him preaching throughout all Galilee, and 1:40 continues the scene with the leper coming to him.

occurred-at:jesus-calls-matthew>capernau.note: The call is by the sea (2:13-14) with no town named; Capernaum is inferred from 2:1. Mark names the caller Levi, not Matthew.

occurred-at:parable-of-the-winseskins>ca.note: The new-wine parable (2:21-22) follows the fasting scene, which names no place. Capernaum is inferred from 2:1.

parent-of:alphaeus_193>matthew_1971@cc38.note: 2:14 says Levi the son of Alphaeus. Mark never calls him Matthew; the Levi-Matthew identity comes from outside Mark.
